questions.stem: The attached Reserve Static Line (RSL) activates the reserve after the main canopy is cut-away and the release of the main risers from the three-ring system. What can occur with RSLs on small, sporty canopies? 1) After a spinning malfunction, the reserve activation may take place in an unstable position. 2) There is no impact with modern systems. 3) The reserve canopy is usually not pulled out completely. 4) The can be problems in particular horseshoe malfunctions

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: You notice that the reserve cable on the reserve handle has no excess length. What can happen? 1) The reserve handle cannot be pulled out of the Velcro pocket. 2) Expansion of the cable housing can lead to reserve activation on opening of the main canopy 3) When boarding and alighting from the aircraft, unwanted activation may occur, 4) That's the way it is meant to be.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: What do I have to pay attention to with reserve handles and cables? 1) The cable must be free to move up to the pin. 2) The reserve cable should have an excess length of approx. 5 cm. 3) The reserve cable must have a stop on the handle side. 4) It must be possible to release the reserve handle from its pocket.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Why are the brakes set when packing? 1) So that the canopy opens in a more controlled manner. 2) To store a larger amount of line material on the risers. 3) To have a smooth opening process, with little forward movement 4) To give the A-lines the right trim.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: What needs to be considered when using a pilot chute with a kill line?

options.text: Nothing, the pilot chute is always ready to jump.
The line must be pulled out in the window and fixed with Velcro
The pilot chute must be cocked before packing and checked later by a throwing test.
Pull out the pilot chute after closing the container.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: What has to be considered when using a pilot chute with bungee system? 1) The pilot chute must consist of zero-P fabric. 2) Mainly used for bungee jumping 3) The bungee must not be shortened without testing. 4) The pilot chute must be cocked before every jump.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: The three-ring system is a very sensitive technical device. 1) It must be moved regularly to maintain its flexibility and mobility. 2) The locking loop may only be passed through the smallest of the three rings, otherwise the power reduction will not work and a tear may occur. 3) The loop must not be damaged. 4) The cable ends of the cut-away cable must not show any breaks, damage or unevenness.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: There are "large" and "small" three-ring systems. How do they differ? 1) The small three-ring system opens more easily. 2) The large three-ring system opens more easily. 3) Under load, the loop of both three-ring systems can be released with low pull-strength thanks to power reduction. 4) Large three-rings are used exclusively on tandem equipment

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: The sensitive point of classic risers with rings on the top is in the area of the grommet for the loop. Which of the following statement(s) applies? 1) Damage is easily recognizable by frayed material. 2) Narrow risers are more susceptible to stress as there is less fabric. 3) This is a predetermined breaking point which protects the harness system in the event of extremely hard or unstable canopy openings. 4) Only the large three-ring system should be used.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: What has to be observed with Velcro fastenings for closing and fastening flaps and steering toggles? 1) The soft component should always cover the entire length of the hook component to avoid damage to the straps, lower steering line section or other components. 2) They can be sources of danger if not regularly maintained. 3) The wear status is indicated by the length of the loops on the soft side. The longer and narrower the loops, the worse the condition of the Velcro. 4) Velcro must be attached with a zigzag seam.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: What problems can occur when using an RSL that is attached only to one riser? 1) If the cut-away cables are of uneven length, there is danger of entangling between main and reserve canopy. 2) The RSL may be incorrectly attached to the three-ring system. 3) To avoid problems, the cut-away pad should always be pulled out quickly and completely. 4) The reserve can be activated via the RSL, although the main canopy is not gone yet.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: What do I check regularly to ensure a smooth cut-away of my main canopy? 1) The smoothness of my three-ring system. 2) The free routing of both cut-away cables 3) The RSL shackle must not be attached to the three-ring system. 4) The correct length ratio of the cut-away cables (important in combination with RSL)

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: The reserve canopy is packed in a freebag with a spring loaded pilot chute that flies away when opened, 1) to prevent a horseshoe malfunction of the reserve canopy. 2) so that the pilot chute clears a parachutist in an unstable position. 3) so it must be caught by the parachutist under the open reserve canopy. 4) so it must be replaced.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: The main canopy has an opening malfunction. Which handles and components are usually no longer there after cutting away and pulling the reserve and can/should be searched for if necessary? 1) The main canopy. 2) The reserve freebag and pilot chute. 3) The cut-away pads and reserve handle. 4) The RSL.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: What are the special design features of a harness with a RAM-air reserve canopy? 1) No connection between freebag and reserve canopy. 2) Long and wide bridle line on freebag. 3) The three-ring system of the reserve risers is particularly smooth-running 4) There are no conventional packing bungees on the freebag.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: The cut-away pad and reserve handle are fixed to the harness so that their position is always the same, 1) therefore the cut-away pad must be peeled from the Velcro before pulling. 2) therefore, the reserve handle must be removed before pulling. 3) the reserve handle must first be pulled out of the Velcro pocket before pulling. 4) applies when operating the handles "right before left".

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: If am under the open reserve canopy, 1) I should expect different flight and flare behaviour. 2) L also have steering toggles like on the main canopy. 3) I follow my cut-away main canopy. 4) I should do a braking and steering exercise.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: For which components (main and reserve canopy, harness and AAD) is a manual available? 1) Only for the harness and the reserve canopy. 2) For the main and reserve canopy. 3) For the automatic activation device. 4) For the harness

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: During a landing you slide two to three meters over asphalt, but you didn't hurt yourself. What is important for your parachute system? 1) The construction webbing, in particular the leg straps, must be checked, as the nylon webbing is very tear-resistant but not abrasion/temperature resistant. 2) The leg straps inside the leg pads should be checked. 3) The container and even the sealed reserve could be damaged. 4) Stop on the runway/road next time.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: What should I bear in mind when using bungees/tubestows to close the deployment bag and stow the lines? 1) Only suitable bungees of the correct size should be used. 2) Suitable tubestows of the right size may be used. Tubestows must not be wrapped around the lines twice. 3) Bungees and tubestows should hold the lines with a certain strength. 4) Tubestows and bungees can be combined as desired.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: What is the risk for a licensed novice parachutist when switching to a small and fast canopy? 1) They are not yet familiar with the opening behaviour. 2) The flare point is different. 3) The turning and landing speed is very high. 4) Endangerment of others through misjudgements.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: The kill line on my canopy system broke. Can I still jump the rest of the day and what should I bear in mind? 1) If the kill line breaks, the canopy system immediately loses its airworthiness and must not be used again. 2) A defective kill line prevents the main canopy from opening properly. 3) A broken kill line has no effect on the opening of the main canopy. 4) Depending on the size of the main canopy, the open pilot chute may affect the flight characteristics.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Where can you find evidence of the last inspection and repack of your system and how frequently must inspections be carried out?

options.text: inspection certificate; for each reserve canopy.
Proof of airworthiness; in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions for the relevant components.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Which components of your parachuting equipment need a pattern test?

options.text: audible altimeter, main canopy, automatic activation device.
all except the automatic activation device.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Why does the equipment have to be carefully placed on a clean packing surface after the jump? 1) So that the AAD does not suffer any damage. 2) Dirt/sand/stones can get into the cable ducts. 3) Metal buckles can get sharp burrs. 4) To treat the canopy as gently as possible

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: You want to pack the canopy and notice that the lines are not running free. What can you do about it?

options.text: Bring a free steering line from the canopy to the toggle in the direction of the harness, where you can solve the tangle by turning the harness accordingly.
Take the D-lines of the middle cell and proceed as in answer a)
Open both three-ring systems, otherwise the lines cannot be sorted.
At the brakes, and then look for the A-lines to be able to sort the B-lines above the cascades.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Why is it important to install slider stoppers on metal Rapide links (Connectorlinks)? 1) To prevent the noise of the slider a stopper is useful. 2) To protect the line attachments on the connector links from the slider grommets when opening. 3) To protect the slider grommets from dents, because sharp edges could damage or even cut the lines when opening. 4) If soft links are used instead of metal connector links, no additional safety devices are required.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Which statement(s) regarding packing is (are) correct? 1) The cell openings at the canopy nose may be rolled for many types of canopies. 2) The further the slider is positioned forward when packing, i.e. towards the nose, the more it slows down the opening. 3) All lines bites should be tight and sufficiently long. 4) Each canopy has a defined opening speed.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Why should the pull-out pad always be in good condition?

options.text: Should it come loose in freefall, I may not find it again.
To be able to pull out the cut-away cables completely.
If the pad does not have the same colour as the jump suit, it must be matched.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: After what period of time should you repack your main canopy before jumping it if it is stored properly and why?

options.text: After about 2 weeks to stay in practice.
According to manufacturer's instructions, after approx. 2 months, for ventilation and to check packing bungees
After approx. 6 months, for ventilation and to check packing bungees.
Once a main canopy has been packed, it can always be jumped, regardless of how long it has been in the deployment bag

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Who may carry out inspections?

options.text: Senior Riggers and Master Riggers (Fallschirmwart/Fallschirmtechniker) in accordance with the manufacturers' instructions.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: How long is the reserve packing interval/inspection interval for harness, reserve canopy and main canopy in Germany?

options.text: According to manufacturer's specifications, usually 1 year.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Who may inspect and pack the reserve of a licensed parachutist? 1) Only the parachutist himself. 2) Master Rigger (Fallschirmtechniker). 3) Senior Rigger (Fallschirmwart). 4) Another licensed parachutist.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Where can I find instructions for the care, maintenance and packing of my harness and canopy? 1) In the manufacturer's manual. 2) In the appendix to the test certificate. 3) In the Technical Operations Manual (TBH). 4) On the last pages of the log book.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Which of the following activities may a licensed parachutist do? 1) Pack his main canopy. 2) Carry out repairs to his parachute system. 3) Jump at all dropzones. 4) Pack the reserve canopy for third parties

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Which of the following activities may a skydiving instructor perform? 1) Pack student canopies. 2) Adjust the size of training harnesses. 3) Pack student reserves. 4) Check students before boarding the plane.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Which of the following activities may a Senior Rigger (Fallschirmwart) perform? 1) Replace original parts in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. 2) Re-line a main canopy. 3) Pack reserve canopies for third parties 4) Pack main canopies for third parties.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Which of the following activities may a Master Rigger (Fallschirmtechniker) perform? 1) Carry out small and large repairs. 2) Determine compatibility in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications. 3) Train Senior Riggers (Fallschirmwart) 4) Certify routine tests and carry out follow-up tests

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: For which disciplines are additional audible altimeters particularly recommended? 1) Accuracy. 2) Headdown and Freefly. 3) Formation Skydiving. 4) Canopy Formation (CRW).

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: What do you have to pay attention to if the take-off airfield and the landing dropzone are at different altitudes about sea level? 1) Adjust visual altimeter and automatic activation device (AAD) for altitude offsets as per their manuals. 2) At extreme altitude differences the flare characteristics of the canopy can be very different. 3) Adjust the audible altimeter. 4) The ground wind can be different.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: What does a parachutist have to consider when relying on a modern audible altimeter? 1) The battery may be flat. 2) It can be overheard. 3) The setting may be wrong. 4) You may have been forgotten to take it with you.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Mechanical altimeters can differ by a few 100m at 4, 000 m/AGL exit height due to their design. What do you do?

options.text: I adapt to the lower height and compare the height to other parachutists in the jump.
Never jump, the altimeter must be defective
I adjust my altimeter to the higher altitude.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: A group of 8 would like to perform an FS jump. Does every parachutist need an altimeter?

options.text: When using chest altimeters, four are sufficient.
Hand altimeters are not recommended here.
Foot altimeters are difficult to read for fellow parachutists

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Is it possible to skydive without a visual altimeter when using an audible altimeter?

options.text: Yes, if it is an electronic device.
Yes, if the warning device is mounted inside the helmet/cap.
No, a visual altimeter should always be used.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: What circumstances require particular attention when using a CYPRES as an AAD? 1) Night jumps, if it was turned on in the morning. 2) Thunderstorms. 3) Landing lower or higher than take off. 4) Water landings if the container was submerged.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: What is the task of an AAD like the CYPRES? 1) Cutting-away the main canopy and activation of the reserve. 2) Only the main canopy is cut away. 3) The reserve is activated. 4) The reserve loop is cut.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: When could a student CYPRES be activated? 1) During certain malfunctions (e.g. streamer), 2) While descending with the aircraft when 13 m/s are exceeded below 300 m/AGL. 3) Above 500 m/AGL at freefall speed. 4) During a radical turn below 300 m/AGL.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: When could an Expert CYPRES be activated? 1) During a demo, if a large difference in take-off and landing site altitude was not considered. 2) During a fast turn below 225 m/AGL at a high wingloading 3) At freefall speed at a height of approx. 225 m/AGL, 4) During a rapid climb in an aircraft from 225 m/AGL altitude.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Is it advisable to do a freefly jump with a parachute system equipped with an FXC 12000 Rev. J?

options.text: Yes, because the FXC is no longer approved for skydiving anyway.
No, because with rapidly changing pressure fluctuations in free fall, a misfire can occur.
Yes, if the battery is not more than one year old, there are no problems.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Can a CYPRES be switched on during the climb to altitude?

options.text: The CYPRES must not be switched on during an ascent.
If you have forgotten it before, you should switch on the device anyway.
Only if the current altitude is continuously corrected on the CYPRES.
No problem, you can simply adopt the set CYPRES height of a fellow parachutist.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: How do I change the setting of the AAD if the take-off and landing areas have different heights above MSL?

options.text: During climb, quickly switch on the apparatus at the appropriate altitude.
Proceed in accordance with the operating instructions.
After switching on, press the button once for each altitude meter.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: If the landing site is 100 m higher than the take-off site, I set the air pressure conditions of

options.text: the CYPRES 100 m higher and the altimeter 100 m lower.
the CYPRES 100 m lower and the altimeter 100 m higher.
the CYPRES 100 m lower and the altimeter 100 m lower.
the CYPRES 100 m higher and the altimeter 100 m higher.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: What has to be considered in case of an high altitude jump (from 4, 000 m/MSL)? 1) For jumps over 13.000 ft MSL (= 4.000 m) an oxygen supply must be available for parachutists. 2) The automatic activation device does not need to be adjusted. 3) The free fall time is longer and the temperature is significantly lower. 4) A preparatory briefing is necessary.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Which terms fall into the category "manual canopy deployment"? 1) Throw-Out. 2) Static line. 3) Ripcord 4) Pull-Out.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: What are the main differences between the throw-out system and the pull-out system? 1) Pull-out system usually has a short bridle, straight pin, grip at the base, pilot chute in the container. 2) Throw-out system usually has long bridle, curved pin, handle on apex, pilot chute mounted outside on container. 3) Both systems have ZP pilot chutes with kill or bungee line, long spiral spring, Velcro fastening system at the BOC. 4) Both terms stand for the same deployment system.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: What should I pay attention to when using a helmet/frap hat? 1) It should not have dangerously sharp edges and comers and have sufficient padding to protect against collisions from exit to landing 2) Possibility of mounting an audible altimeter. 3) A video helmet should have an emergency cut-away system with pilot chute. 4) Should be secured with chinstrap for tight fit and against loss.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: What do you have to pay attention to when jumping with a different kind of jumpsuit (Wingsuit, Freefly, Video)? 1) That the cut-away pad and reserve handle are not covered. 2) Changed flight behaviour in free fall and when pulling. 3) Suit colour and cut-away pad colour should not be identical 4) That I am clearly recognizable in freefall.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: What in particular should be considered when using a wingsuit? 1) The different flight behaviour requires precise instruction. 2) The low fall rate can lead to the AAD not being activated. If possible, use suitable AAD. 3) Reaching all handles and deploying the main canopy may be difficult. 4) A significantly higher horizontal speed can endanger others.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Which functions should shoes (not just during ground training) and gloves fulfil when jumping? 1) The sense of grip must be maintained despite the gloves. 2) Good fit. 3) Protection of hands and feet. 4) Fleece on the palms of the gloves and coarse profile soles are useful.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Which components or parts do not belong on a student harness?

options.text: Dive loops/loops on the main front risers.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: What has to be considered when using round canopies? 1) They have little forward speed and are not that controllable. 2) You don't have a slider. 3) They cannot be braked. 4) You don't have a freebag.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: What should canopies and harnesses be cleaned or rinsed with? 1) With benzine. 2) Clean with clean fresh water or rinse thoroughly after landing in salt water. 3) With gentle dry-cleaning agents (e.g. gall soap). 4) Clean with clean salt water and rinse if necessary, dry in the sun, treat salt and dirt residues with a coarse brush.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: What colour is the seal thread of a packed reserve canopy?

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Which materials are used in skydiving? 1) Cordura, Parapack 2) Dacron, Spectra 3) ZP, F-111 4) Grommets in sizes 0, 2, 4 and 8

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Why are nylon lines unsuitable for a RAM-air canopy?

options.text: They are still used for older accuracy canopies.
The frictional heat from the slider would melt them.
Nylon is too expensive to produce.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Which components belong to a RAM-air canopy? 1) Deployment bag with pilot chute and bridle. 2) Slider, lines, stabilizers, crossports. 3) Connectors, cells with crossports, stabilizers, slider, bridle attachment point, 4) risers, deployment bag, BOC.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Which components belong to a harness?

options.text: Main and reserve canopies, automatic activation device, pilot chute
Leg, chest and shoulder straps, deployment bag with pilot chute, main and reserve risers with steering loops, bridle, pack trays, cut-away pad and reserve handle.
Deployment bags without pilot chutes, hook knife, connectors, reserve canopy.
chest mounted reserve, altimeter holder, manufacturer's emblem.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Can all components (main and reserve canopy, harness and AAD) be combined in any way? 1) No, the respective manufacturers must agree to the compatibility. 2) The sizes of the main and reserve canopies must fit into the harness/container system. 3) AADs of any kind may be installed in any harness without any problems. 4) The components can of course be combined as desired.

options.text: Only answers 2, 3 and 4 are correct. TH99

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Can the line trim of my canopy change? 1) The line trim changes minimally with each jump. 2) The lines at the edge of the canopy and the steering lines shrink. 3) The lines in the middle of the canopy stretch. 4) The line trim on the canopy does not change.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: How can I tell that the line trim of my canopy has changed? 1) The opening, flying and flare behaviour of my canopy gets worse. 2) The line trim can be measured on the ground. 3) The change of the line trim is not detectable by a parachutist. 4) The stall point of my canopy changes.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Which rule of thumb can be used to convert kg into lbs?

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: What is the function of MARD systems (Main Assisted Reserve Deployment) such as Skyhook or Rax systems?

options.text: The MARD system opens the reserve container after a cut-away and thus initiates the reserve opening.
With a connecting line between RSL and the Bridle of the reserve, the reserve is pulled out by the main canopy flying away immediately after cutting away.
A connection between the cut-away pad and the reserve handle automatically pulls the reserve handle after a cut-away.
MARD systems measure the air pressure and open the reserve container when the release criteria are met.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Which statements on MARD systems are correct? 1) The MARD system may pose a problem in case of a canopy collisions. 2) If the RSL is disconnected, the MARD system will not work. 3) In the event of a total malfunction, the MARD system cannot activate the reserve. The activation must be carried out manually using the reserve handle. 4) The functionality of MARD systems cannot be checked 100 % from the outside.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: The permanent height adjustment of the Cypres 2 allows the release height to be set 30 m higher in 9 steps. Which statements are correct? 1) There are no reasons for a higher adjustment of the Cypres 2. 2) Due to newer designs of harness and reserve canopies the opening distance of a reserve may be longer. 3) If the release height is increased, the risk of 2-canopies out increases. 4) The opening height of the main canopy should be raised sensibly.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Where can I get information about safety advisories, technical advisories, etc. for my canopy system from?

options.text: From the manufacturer of the respective components, technical /rigging staff and the relevant parachute associations.
From EASA and the Federal Aviation Authority.
For foreign products, from the respective national aviation authority.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Who is responsible for staying informed about safety messages etc.?

options.text: The manufacturer will unilaterally inform all keepers.
The technical /rigging staff will inform the keeper.
EASA and foreign aeronautical authorities will inform the operator.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Who is responsible for the airworthiness of the canopy system between inspections?

options.text: The owner of the canopy jump system.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Which components (reserve canopies and harnesses) can I jump in Germany? This which are: 1) type-approved. 2) accredited. 3) are unit-tested and have a valid verification certificate. 4) have been type-tested and are listed in the type register 64 [...].

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Who can certify unit tests? 1) Senior Riggers (Fallschirmwart) and Master Riggers (Fallschirmtechniker). 2) For foreign products only a Master Rigger (Fallschirmtechniker). 3) Master Riggers (Fallschirmtechniker) only. 4) For domestic products only the canopy manufacturer.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: Who is allowed to assemble a new parachute system for the first time?

options.text: The manufacturer, Master Riggers (Fallschirmtechniker) according to the manufacturer's instructions

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: The certificate of airworthiness of the main canopy, reserve canopy or harness-container system is completed, and a follow-up document has been created by the technical /rigging staff. What do I do with the old certificate of airworthiness?

options.text: The old certificate of airworthiness may be disposed of.
The old certificate of airworthiness should be sent to the manufacturer to inform them of the condition of the components.
I keep the old airworthiness certificate with the papers to ensure a complete proof (e.g.: safety information, technical notes, etc.).
I can do what I want with the old certificate of airworthiness.

questions.subject: Equipment
questions.stem: A canopy system no longer meets the airworthiness criteria. What do I as the owner have to do independently of the fact that the system may no longer be jumped?

options.text: I must inform the manufacturer and the relevant parachute association.
I must inform the relevant parachute association.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: "Behaviour in special circumstances" deals with raising awareness and accident prevention. What does this mean in practice?

options.text: Knowing that skydiving is associated with risks.
Sources of danger must be identified to determine appropriate safe behaviour.
emergency procedures are designed to be executed in the time or altitude available and are not intended to identify the root cause of the problem

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: How do you land a RAM-air canopy?

options.text: Straight flight, canopy parallel to the ground.
Land with brakes (in a flare), if necessary, make a parachute landing fall.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: In which direction is it most sensible to plan a landing?

options.text: At right angles to the wind.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: How does one land a RAM-air parachute downwind?

options.text: Land in a full flare, if necessary, execute parachute landing fall and/or slide the landing in.
Wait while the brakes are applied.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: How should one react when landing downwind of an obstacle?

options.text: Expect an increased fall rate, flare fully to land, execute a parachute landing fall if necessary.
Release steering toggles and prepare for a stand-up landing.
Continue to sink unbraked, prepare for landing.
Start a turn and land with a full flare.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: What should a parachutist expect if he suddenly releases both control toggles of his strongly braked canopy shortly before landing?

options.text: a violent oscillation towards the ground and thus a high risk of injury.
a collapse of the end cells.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: You notice that you flared about 15-20 m too early, What should you do now?

options.text: Continue to descend in the full flare.
Let the steering lines back up to the top quickly.
Slowly lift the steering lines up to approx. shoulder height and brake again at the right time.
Keep the canopy under control by pumping,

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: What posture can result in serious injury during a landing?

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: What common error can cause injury during landing?

options.text: Preparation for a parachute landing fall.
Pull both steering lines all the way down.
Uneven flare (canopy tilts to one side).

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: What action should be taken if, for any reason, you have turned too low for the landing approach?

options.text: The turn must be completed in order to take advantage of the full flare.
Stop the turn immediately and flare sooner.
Cut-away the canopy immediately and try to roll the landing off.
Initiate a turn in the opposite direction and flare.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: What possibilities do you have to improvise during a landing which is not quite going to plan?

options.text: If the landing is fast despite flare and parallel to the ground, I can possibly slide better than run it out.
If the descent is directly downward, I should definitely land with a parachute landing fall.
In the case of an unconventional landing, it is always advisable to keep your legs firmly together or never support yourself on the ground with your hands.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: What should I bear in mind when landing in unknown terrain?

options.text: release the RSL, the preparation of the parachute landing fall.
Obstacles, ground conditions and wind influence.
Landing close to a telephone box in order to be able to call the dropzone.
land normally and the recover the canopy.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist lands in a strong wind, What should they to pay attention to?

options.text: Stand up the landing and wait for wind to die down.
Immediately kneel down and hold on to the canopy.
Both steering lines should be stowed if you are being dragged.
Immediately after landing, turn around and pull in one steering line.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: After landing, a parachutist is being dragged over the ground by their open canopy. What measures should he take immediately?

options.text: Turn on his back, pull in a steering line.
Stay still, not pull in any of the steering lines.
Stand up, pull in the steering lines.
Turn on his back and wait.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A skydiver got injured during landing and is being dragged over the ground. How can he stop being dragged as quickly as possible?

options.text: If necessary, disconnect the RSL and cut-away the main canopy.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist lands on a building with a flat roof and is dragged towards the edge of the roof due to stronger winds. What action should he take?

options.text: Stay in place until the canopy falls over the edge of the roof.
If necessary, disconnect the RSL and immediately cut-away the main canopy.
Get up immediately and try to walk around the canopy.
Get up immediately and try to hold on to the canopy.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A landing on a flat roof is unavoidable. How does the skydiver behave?

options.text: Land normally, secure the canopy immediately, loosen RSL if necessary and cut away canopy if there is a strong wind.
Do the parachute landing fall especially carefully and call for assistance.
land and climb down from the roof immediately.
Land in a standing position, open the reserve and abseil on the lines.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: What should be avoided in any case during a water landing?

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: When does a parachutist cuts away his main canopy during a water landing?

options.text: After the landing in the water.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: If you land in the water under your main canopy, you should behave as follows: 1) After immersing yourself in the water, cut-away the main canopy. 2) Dive away from the main canopy and do not recover any equipment. 3) Remove the harness and use the closed reserve for a short time as a buoyancy aid if necessary. 4) Hold the left arm above water to avoid damaging the altimeter.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: After a malfunction, you cut-away the main canopy and pulled the reserve. Due to the lower opening height, a water landing on the reserve canopy is unavoidable. How do you behave? 1) Dive with fill equipment after the freebag. 2) Immediately remove the harness from the water and dive away from the canopy system. 3) If possible, fly as close as possible to the nearest shore. 4) Cut the lines with the canopy knife.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A tree landing is unavoidable. How do you position the canopy if possible?

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: What should you do after a tree landing if there is no ground contact?

options.text: Open the harness and jump down.
Stay stuck without any movement and wait for help.
Try to reach the tree trunk by swinging.
Disconnect the main canopy and pull the reserve.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A tree landing is unavoidable. Which posture should I adopt?

options.text: Do not adopt a particular posture. Loosen chest and leg straps.
Sit low in the harness, spread legs, activate reserve.
Hold legs firmly together, press elbows in front of chest, hold hands in front of face.
Continue steering and ignore the tree

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: What should one do if one finds a safe hold on the trunk after a tree landing?

options.text: Remove the canopy, climb down with the canopy.
Hold on to the trunk and wait for help.
Cut the canopy away and climb down.
Open the harness and jump down.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: How can a parachutist tell if there are power lines in the terrain?

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist flies towards a power line. How should he behave?

options.text: Tur the canopy into the wind and continue flying with the brakes on.
Avoid them if possible, otherwise try to fly along the lines.
Fly with the wind and if necessary, pull up the legs.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: Contact with a high-voltage line under canopy is unavoidable. What position should be taken?

options.text: Legs together, elbows in front of the chest, hands in front of the face (do not release the steering toggles).
Legs together, arms down, filly braked.
arms apart to cause a short circuit as far as possible.
Position unchanged, preparation for a harder landing.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: During a landing a power line was cut. What do I have to consider? 1) The cable is currentless after tearing and therefore harmless. 2) Call the police and/or power station. 3) The current is switched on again after a short time and becomes an additional danger. 4) A minimum distance of 20 metres must be maintained for helpers

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist can only land on a slope. What landing procedure is best?

options.text: With the wind and down the slope.
Across the slope, fully braked, parachute landing fall.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: Landing on a road is unavoidable. How's the skydiver supposed to land?

options.text: Land normally, ask passers-by for transport possibilities.
Land normally, if necessary, parachute landing fall and clear road immediately.
Fly with the wind and prepare for a harder landing,
Prepare for harder landing and pack canopy immediately.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A landing on a pitched roof is unavoidable. How does the skydiver behave?

options.text: Slide down the roof, open the reserve canopy and prepare for a hard landing.
Fly diagonally to the roof in a steep curve and look for a foothold.
Brake normally, seek immediate stop on touchdown and wait for help if necessary.
Brake strongly, approach as steeply as possible to the roof pitch.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist lands on a railroad track. How must he behave?

options.text: Drop the canopy and leave the railway immediately.
Leave the railway immediately with the canopy.
Mark the canopy and alert the train. 4d) Pick up the canopy properly and slowly leave the track.
Pick up the canopy properly and slowly leave the track.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist jumps in mountains. What must he pay special attention to? 1) The wind conditions. 2) Windward and leeward effects. 3) The beautiful view. 4) The correct exit point.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist jumps into a valley. Which part of the valley should he avoid?

options.text: The leeward side of the valley.
The windward side of the valley.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist jumps in the mountains. What should he always expect? 1) low temperatures. 2) sudden turbulences. 3) faster fallrate due to the higher altitude. 4) high temperatures.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist lands on a runway. How must he behave?

options.text: Drop the canopy and leave the runway immediately.
Mark the canopy and alert the pilot.
Pick up the canopy properly and leave the runway slowly.
Immediately leave the runway with your canopy.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: The jump plane has to stop the climb and land again with the parachutists. How should the parachutist behave?

options.text: he should aim to be the first to leave the aeroplane as quickly as possible
After landing, the parachutist remains seated with his seat belt fastened until the skydiving operation manager orders him to leave.
Buckle up, helmet on for landing. Do not leave the aircraft towards the propeller on landing.
He must hold on to the other parachutists during the landing.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: Why does it make sense to wear head protection during take-off? 1) To look as professional as possible. 2) To protect yourself in the event of an aborted take-off. 3) To protect the fellow skydivers from the flying headgear (helmet/frap hat) in case of an aborted take-off. 4) To identify yourself as a student.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist notices shortly before the jump that his container has opened. What should he do?

options.text: Take the canopy under his arm and jump immediately.
Pack the canopy during the climb with an open container.
Alert the pilot and try to jump with the open container.
Secure the canopy, loosen RSL if necessary, disconnect main canopy, notify pilot and land with airplane.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A skydiver notices shortly before the jump that the pilot chute of a fellow skydiver has partially slipped out of the BOC What should he do?

options.text: immediately draw the attention of the other parachutist to this fact.
behaves quietly, as it has no influence on his jump.
notifies the pilot and arranges an immediate landing.
does not say anything to avoid disturbing other parachutists.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: Which check should be done shortly before a jump? 1) Check whether chest and leg straps are correctly closed and sufficiently tight. 2) Check that all handles are in place and reachable in the correct order. 3) Check that all additional equipment (helmet, glasses, altimeter, etc.) is in place. 4) Check that the main and reserve containers are still properly closed.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: In the exit position, the main canopy of a parachutist opens unintentionally. He is torn out of the door and gets stuck on the plane by his canopy. What should he not do in this situation?

options.text: Cut away the main canopy and then pull reserve.
Give the ok. sign and initiate the emergency procedure after a parachutist who is still in the aircraft has cut him off if necessary.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist is getting ready to jump out of the plane. His reserve canopy opens and enters the airstream. What action must he take immediately?

options.text: Jump immediately, regardless of the correct exit position.
Retract and hold the reserve canopy.
Call the pilot and hold the reserve canopy.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist gets tangled up with a safety belt in the plane without realizing it. What serious consequence can this have?

options.text: get caught on the aeroplane and/or get injured.
Tearing off the wrist mounted altimeter.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: Immediately before the jump, a parachutist notices that his three-ring system is not correctly attached. How does he behave?

options.text: He remains seated and lands with the airplane.
He jumps and pulls the reserve.
He jumps and tries to correct the error.
He ask the other parachutists to assist him with correcting the mistake.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist with a video helmet notices 2 minutes before the jump that he has a problem with his camera. What is the priority now?

options.text: First check the complete jump equipment as usual, then check the camera, if necessary, jump without the video on.
Try to get the camera up and running until the jump, demand a second run-in if necessary.
Keep other video parachutists from preparing to jump and ask for help.
Quickly change the battery, force a restart of the camera if necessary and jump without the equipment safety check due to the obvious lack of time.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: Immediately after take-off, the engine of the skydiving aircraft stops. When attempting an emergency landing, the aircraft overturns. There are no casualties. How do the skydivers behave?

options.text: leave the aeroplane only at the request of the pilot.
leave the aeroplane only after helpers have arrived.
leave the aeroplane immediately one after the other.
leave the aeroplane only after consulting the flight controller.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: After take-off the engine of the jump aircraft fails at 250 m/AGL. How should the skydivers behave?

options.text: Jump and immediately deploy the canopy.
Jump and immediately disconnect the main canopy and pull the reserve.
Jump and immediately deploy the main canopy and then pull the reserve canopy additionally.
Remain seated in the aircraft with your seat belt fastened and assume the crash position.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A group of skydivers must perform an emergency jump between 300-800 m/AGL away from the dropzone. How do they behave?

options.text: Pull the reserve directly 1 sec after exit, look for a safe place to land.
Maintain a staggered flight pattern (stack), stay together and head for a common place to land.
Fall freely at will and look for a place to land.
Maintain the staggered flight pattern (stack), allow reserve to pass through AAD and land safely.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: Immediately after take-off, the engine of the skydiving aircraft stops. When attempting an emergency landing, the aircraft overturns. There are parachutists in the aircraft with static lines and without. There are no casualties. How do the skydivers behave?

options.text: Once the parachutists without static lines have left the aeroplane, unhook and remove the static lines.
When leaving the aircraft, make sure that the parachutists leave the aircraft alternately static line/non-static line
Immediately unhook or cut the static lines in order to leave the aeroplane as quickly as possible.
Only leave the aeroplane after assistance has reached the aeroplane and the static lines have been unhooked.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist jumps with a high temperature. Which of the following statements applies? 1) As long as he takes the right medication there is no danger. 2) His reaction capacity is impaired. 3) A nasal spray always allows a problem-free jump. 4) It can lead to severe headaches and toothaches in freefall.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist injures his right hand during the exit and cannot open his canopy. What should he do?

options.text: extend free fall and try to pull with the left hand.
pull the reserve with the left hand.
wait for the automatic activation device to deploy the reserve.
make a formation jump and have his main canopy pulled by a fellow skydiver.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist suffers cardiac issues during the climb. How should he behave?

options.text: Ask the pilot to climb more slowly.
Jump immediately and initiate the opening procedure
Alert the pilot to his condition and request him to land.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: After pulling the main canopy, the parachutist notices that his canopy is not stable, and that the descent speed is still very high. What do you call this malfunction?

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: After pulling the main canopy, one or more lines are over the canopy after deployment, What is this malfunction called?

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist opens his canopy in an unstable position. What can he expect?

options.text: The opening process is not normal. A malfunction may occur.
The canopy opens after a longer delay.
The canopy opens normally, but sideways from the parachutist.
There is a rollover and a normal opening of the canopy.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: After pulling the main canopy, the container remains closed. What do you call this malfunction?

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: After pulling the pilot chute, the parachutist does not notice any reaction of the canopy. What action should he take first?

options.text: Check altitude, shake body briefly, change freefall position, emergency procedure if necessary.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: After pulling the pilot chute, the lines are stretched, but the deployment bag is not released. That's why the canopy won't open. What do you call this malfunction?

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: When is the emergency procedure initiated in the event of a total malfunction?

options.text: After a waiting period of several seconds.
After 1-2 attempts to eliminate the total malfunction, at the latest at 500 m/AGL.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist wants to open his canopy and can't find his new toggle: What should he do first?

options.text: Pull reserve immediately and prepare for particularly hard landing
Change position and initiate the opening by striking the outer packaging.
Pull the reserve, then try to cut-away the main canopy and expect a hard landing.
Search again for the toggle, check free fall postion and altitude, initiate emergency procedure in case of failure.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: The canopy only partially opened. The parachutist sinks quickly and turns in one direction. What action is required?

options.text: Remove the malfunction by pulling the rear risers
Eliminate the malfunction by releasing a brake.
Check altitude, possibly one or two pumps, if necessary emergency procedure
Wait until the canopy flies calmly.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: The canopy only partially opened. The parachutist is in a fast spin, which makes him lose his orientation immediately. How should he behave?

options.text: If pumping once or twice does not solve the problem, check altitude, cut-away the main canopy and open the reserve.
Close your eyes and quietly count to ten.
Immediately counteract with the front risers

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist opens the reserve canopy. How do the other parachutists behave in his immediate vicinity? They 1) inform the manifest. 2) keep distance and avoid any obstruction. 3) observe the canopy and the freebag to get as much information as possible about the landing site. 4) land as close as possible to the parachutist, if your performance level allows it.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: After opening a parachutist is back to front under canopy. What should he do?

options.text: Turn the main riser and continue flying
Return to the normal position by doing a rollover in the harness.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: While the canopy is being deployed, the bridle line of the pilot chute gets entangled with the body of the parachutist. What action should be taken if the attempt to release the bridle was unsuccessful?

options.text: Start a turn, minimize the body position, pull the reserve.
Pull the risers and both steering lines simultaneously.
Pull the main risers apart and wait until the entanglement is released.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: After opening the canopy at a sufficient altitude, the lines are strongly twisted. The canopy flies straight ahead. How to react?

options.text: Pull the steering lines and pump.
Release the toggles from half-breaks and pull down on one side.
Actively untwist while keeping an eye on the height, emergency procedure if necessary.
Release the toggles from half-brakes and let go.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: The slider gets stuck directly undemeath the canopy. How can this problem usually be solved?

options.text: Grabbing onto the risers and initiating a turn.
Simultaneously pulling both steering lines or the rear risers several times (pumping).
alternately pulling the right-hand steering line and the left-hand steering line.
pulling on the front risers and release both steering lines simultaneously.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: Two cells are not filled on the right side of the canopy. How can I resolve this problem?

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: The left steering line breaks on the canopy. In which direction does the canopy turn and how does one react to this problem?

options.text: Left. Check altitude, cut-away and pull reserve.
Right. Release right steering line and steer with both rear risers, check flight behaviour and landability, if necessary, initiate emergency procedure
Right. Pull down both rear risers evenly until landing.
Left. Do not take action and prepare for harder landing.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: By flying in the wake vortex of a RAM-air parachute flying ahead, the canopy collapses on the left side. What actions should be taken?

options.text: Open the canopy by pulling the left steering line strongly.
Open the canopy by pulling both steering lines strongly (pumps)
Shift the body weight and initiate counter rotation.
Check altitude, cut-away and pull reserve.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: After opening the canopy, the lines are strongly twisted, the canopy starts a fast tun immediately. What difficulties can this cause? 1) The centrifugal force makes it impossible for the parachutist to untwist, he must immediately initiate the emergency procedure (possibly increased force is to be expected for pulling the handles). 2) If the parachutist remains in the turn without reaction, he will soon lose his orientation and possibly even his altitude awareness. 3) The altimeter will display an incorrect value. 4) The lines will be tom by the strong friction.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: Several lines break during the opening. Which of the following statements are correct? 1) If the canopy passes the brake and steering test, you can land it. 2) If there are more than two broken lines, always pull the reserve. 3) In case of a line break you must always cut-away and pull reserve. 4) If the canopy does not pass the brake and steering test, the emergency procedure must be initiated.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: When a canopy is opened, a brake toggle is released on one side. How do you behave?

options.text: Check altitude, cut-away and pull reserve.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: When flying over land a parachutist encounters violent turbulence. What can he expect?

options.text: no degradation of the flight condition.
a significant increase in forward speed.
a collapse of the outer cells or even of the whole canopy.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A RAM-air canopy was stalled unintentionally by flight manoeuvres in deep brakes. How can this situation be solved at sufficient altitude?

options.text: Sudden release of the steering lines.
Additional pull down of the rear risers.
Slowly letting up the steering lines again symmetrically.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: After a formation jump, the canopies open at a short distance from each other. How to behave?

options.text: Release the brakes and fly away slowly.
Wait for other parachutists to take action.
Steer away immediately with the rear main risers

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: Why should even an experienced parachutist do a flare test after opening their canopy? Which statement is correct?

options.text: The flare test may be dispensed if the opening is smooth.
A flare test is required only after minor and serious malfunctions have been corrected.
In order to check whether a canopy can be landed safely, the flare test must always be made.
As an experienced parachutist, I can visually judge whether I can land the canopy safely.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: During the run-in to the exit spot it suddenly starts to rain heavily. How should the skydivers behave?

options.text: disregard the weather change and jump.
initiate a new run-in and jump.
abort the approach and land in the aeroplane.
descend to 500 m/AGL in the aeroplane and perform an emergency jump.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist performs a jump in the mountains, What negative side effects must he expect at medium wind speeds?

options.text: With considerable up and down drafts

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: The wind has picked up. A parachutist does not reach the planned landing area and prepares for a landing between higher obstacles (buildings, halls). What wind conditions must he expect?

options.text: turbulence and increase in wind speed.
gustiness controllable by pendulum landing technique

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: Why does it make sense to check the wind situation again shortly before boarding the plane?

options.text: To give this information to the pilot at take-off.
To be sure that I have to look into the windsock when landing.
Inorder to be able to derive the landing direction from the landing site in the event of an off landing
To radio the wind situation to the manifest.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A landing is planned behind an approximately 20 m high forest in flat terrain (meadow). At what distance from the obstacle (forest) do the vortices dissolve?

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: On an otherwise level terrain there is an obstacle in the form of a barn. What kind of vortices on the leeward side can you expect?

options.text: More horizontal vortex formation (change of wind direction).

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist was slightly injured during landing. What should I do?

options.text: Provide first aid, keep the jump operation running.
Stop the jump operation and notify the police.
Leave the parachutist lying down, request a rescue helicopter.
Continue the jump operation and prohibit the slightly injured from jumping.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist was seriously injured during landing. What immediate actions should be taken?

options.text: Stop jumping and immediately transport the seriously injured person to the hospital.
Take photographs, securing the canopy and interviewing the injured person.
Provide first aid, notify the flight controller and emergency services and, if necessary, interrupt the jump operation.
Carry away the injured persons, allow jump operation again and notify the police.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: If you exit ahead of the landing area (approach against the wind), it is best to fly:

options.text: sideways to the direction of the landing area and wait until the canopies of the parachutists who have left the aircraft afterwards are open.
to the west (because that's where the wind usually comes from).
away from the landing area and prepare for an off landing,

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A parachutist performs a jerky turn on his open canopy with a steering line, followed by an immediate abrupt counter turn, What can he expect?

options.text: With a stall of the canopy.
Definitely not a pendulum deflection due to mass inertia.
Induction of twists in the lines and jamming of the steering lines in the twist.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: According to statistics, what causes the most fatal accidents in parachuting? 1) Use of faulty material. 2) Canopy collisions. 3) Opening problems. 4) Turning too low on landing.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: A skydiver borrows a canopy system from another skydiver. What should he be informed about and instructed in order to avoid problems? 1) About the validity of the airworthiness certificates of all components 2) About the valid reserve pack (Senior/Master Rigger). 3) About size and type of the main and reserve canopy and type of AAD. 4) About the type of opening system.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: Spirals are a popular manoeuvre on canopies but should be performed with caution. What's the danger? 1) The parachutist easily loses track of the airspace, this can lead to canopy collisions. 2) The parachutist gets a little nauseous. 3) The lines wear prematurely. 4) The lower parachutists may not be able to see the parachutist approaching from above, which can lead to canopy collisions.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: What are the typical circumstances of canopy collisions? 1) Lack of airspace control 2) Spiral turns. 3) Uneven landing directions 4) Broken steering lines.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: After the opening of your main canopy your reserve canopy opens behind it. Both canopies now stand one behind the other and are fully open in a bi-plane situation. What do you do??

options.text: Do not release toggles off half-brakes, steer carefully with the rear risers of the main canopy, do not flare during landing, perform parachute landing fall.
Carefilly release the brakes on the main canopy, check the reserve and then steer with both canopies.
Release the brakes on the main and reserve canopies and fly with both canopies alternately steering to the landing. area.
Wait how both canopy canopies behave, release the brakes on the reserve canopy, steer with the main canopy.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: After a total malfunction you activate your RAM-air reserve without having cut-away the main canopy first. Suddenly your main canopy opens and stands next to the open reserve canopy in a side-by-side situation without further entanglement. What do you do?

options.text: Check the canopies, disconnect the RSL if necessary, cut-away the main canopy and land with the reserve.
Ignore the reserve canopy and control your descent with the main canopy.
If possible, bring both canopies back together and land.
Release the brakes of the reserve canopy and steer it to the landing site.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: During the canopy opening the reserve was additionally activated and the two canopies are in a down plane situation. How must the parachutist behave?

options.text: Use the reserve steering toggles to bring the canopies back under control.
Wait, because down plan situations dissolve quickly.
Release the RSL, cut away the main canopy quickly.
Use the steering toggles of the main canopy to bring the canopies back under control.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: You had a canopy collision right after a normal opening at 800 meters. Your canopy got mixed up with another parachutist's canopy. What do you do?

options.text: Check altitude, cut-away and pull reserve.

Check altitude, take measures only after agreement with the other parachutist (e.g. lower parachutist cuts away and pulls reserve, while the upper parachutist continues flying and assesses the situation)
Try to achieve a bi-plane situation by active steering and land.
Both parachutists pull the reserves at the same time without cutting away in order to achieve as much braking effect as possible.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: After the canopy opens, the parachutist hangs with his legs in the lines (Flamingo situation). What to do?

options.text: The canopy flies anyway. The parachutist can land this and then release himself from the lines.
Do not release the toggles off half-brakes and steer the canopy with your legs.
Immediately cut-away and pull the reserve.
Attempt to resolve. The canopy may be landable. If not, initiate altitude-adjusted emergency procedure.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: What are the main risks of a night jump?

options.text: The visual flight rules can only be respected to a limited extent; the landing area cannot be inspected.
Danger of collision in freefall and under canopy due to restricted visibility, misjudging during landing.
The exit is missed, the jump is carried out too hesitantly, the landing area is missed due to a lack of lighting.
The jump in the air is carried out too hectically, the batteries of the night equipment discharge quickly in free fall.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: What should be considered with demo jumps?

options.text: Demo equipment should be attached to the harness in such a way that it can be shown in free fall, it shall be released during the landing approach.
Demo equipment shall be activated prior to the jump and shall be placed so that it does not interfere with the jump or disturb other parachutists.
Demo devices must be shown to the public immediately after the opening of the canopy and must be specifically dropped during the landing approach.
The demo equipment shall not interfere with the functioning of the opening system. They must be secured against falling off.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: What should be considered with flag jumps?

options.text: They must be attached to the body in such a way that the spectators can see them. They may not be dropped until landing.
Flags shall in principle be carried in a suitable container and shall be detached at least 50 m above the ground on landing.
They shall be secured against falling off and shall not interfere with the functioning of the opening system. You're reducing the forward speed.
Flags are only to be shown in free fall and should be cut away immediately after the opening of the canopy, because they can get entangled with the main canopy.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: You're being filmed by a videographer. What needs to be discussed before the jump?

options.text: The jump order: The video man jumps last, flies under the formation and opens his canopy last.
technical film measures: Backlight should be avoided (do not fly in the sun) Shutter speeds should be set.
Checking the video setting on exit: The number of formations to be recorded in freefall and the freefall time.
The exit position, the separation height, the separation behaviour, the videoman must not be directly above a parachutist.

questions.subject: Behaviour in Special Circumstances
questions.stem: How can the danger of a canopy collision be reasonably minimized?

options.text: By good horizontal separation during formation jumping, waving off before opening, foresighted and attentive flight behaviour under canopy.
Keep to the prescribed opening height at the dropzone, clean separation or tracking away. After opening the canopy, take the shortest way to the landing area.
By clean opening behaviour after clear agreement of the opening height and an immediate height reduction after the canopy opening.
By clean separation of the formations. Do not open the canopy too high and immediately after opening orient it towards the landing area and head for it
